external\\usaspending-api\\usaspending_a.content: Basic USAspending API Training Introduction to APIs State profile GET request Advanced Search POST Request Agenda Additional challenges and resources Questions When to use the API? Introduction What is an API? to APIs GET vs POST requests When to use the API? The USAspending API powers all functionality on the website. Anything you can do on the site, you can do in the API. The API has some functionality not available on the site. For many simple and one-off tasks it’s often easier to use the website. • Consider using the USAspending API if… • You need functionality which is only available through the API. • You want to automate a report you need to run periodically. • You want to automate repetitive tasks which would otherwise require manual work on the website. • You want to build a workflow that allows you to do more of your tasks in tools like Excel. What is an API? What is an API? 2 The backend team transforms the raw ingredients (data) into more simple and digestible formats. The frontend team designs beautiful ways to present the data to help humans consume it and gain insights. APIs bridge this gap by providing the data curated by the backend team in a standard format for presentation on the website, or other tools. What is an API? 3 USAspending uses REST API endpoints to transfer formatted data from the server to client browsers. A REST API endpoint uses a set of defined rules to share or access this formatted data through an HTTP request. USAspending endpoints each present different data elements with different levels of aggregation and enable different sets of filters. For example, the set of endpoints used to power state profile pages is different from the set of endpoints used to power advanced search. Notes: https://stackoverflow.com/a/18768849 GET vs POST Requests • GET and POST are two different types of REST API requests. • Certain endpoints require you to use either a GET or POST request. • This is included in the documentation for each endpoint. • GET requests are used to get data on a specific record with a known numerical identifier. • GET requests also support simple filtering. • A count of new awards for an agency in a single fiscal year • POST requests are used in USAspending to support more advanced filtering. • All grants that were awarded to a specific congressional district in a specific fiscal year from a specific agency How much money went to my state in a FY? Steps: 1. Navigate to a state profile page on USAspending to State profile see the total award amount in a period. 2. Inspect the page to identify which endpoint is used to GET display this number. 3. Review the endpoint documentation. Requests 4. Adjust the GET request URL for a different state or time period. 5. Replicate this GET request in Excel. NOTE: The images and values in the following screenshots may appear different on your system. GET Request - Demo Navigate to the CA state profile page on USAspending: https://www.usaspending.gov/s tate/california/latest Observe the Total Award Amount value. Right click the CA profile page and click Inspect. (or use hotkey Command + Control + c on mac or Control + Shift + c on PC) Demo continued 1 Select the Network tab and refresh the page. Demo continued 2 Use the filter box to only show API calls to api.usaspending.gov Demo continued 3 Select the api/v2/recipient/state/06 API request. Observe the Request URL and Request Method. Demo continued 4 Open the Request URL in your browser. Compare the total_prime_amount and the Total Awarded Amount. GET Request – Demo 2 https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/recipient/state/06/?year=latest • The “/06/” in the URL specifies a state by FIPS code (CA in this case) • The “?year=latest” filters the data filters the data to the trailing 12 months Try changing the “06” to a different FIPS code. Try changing the year filter to 2022. Demo continued 5 In Excel, select Data > Get Data > From Other Sources > From Web Demo continued 6 Paste your GET request URL into the URL box and click OK. Demo continued 7 Compare the request results table to the CA profile page on USAspending. Click 'Into Table' Demo continued 8 Select 'Close and Load' Demo continued 9 Your data is now populated in an Excel spreadsheet! How much did my Congressional District receive in a FY? Advanced Steps: Search 1. Find this number using USAspending Advanced Search. POST 2. Inspect the page to identify which endpoints are used to display this number on the webpage. Request 3. Review the documentation for this endpoint. 4. Use PowerQuery to reproduce this API request in Excel. Demo continued 10 Create an advanced search with a time period and recipient location filter. Demo continued 12 Right click the page and select Inspect. Demo continued 13 Observe the network resources the browser is using to power the page. Demo continued 14 Use the filter box to only show API calls to api.usaspending.gov Demo continued 15 Select the map tab in USAspending Advanced Search and select Recipient Location and Congressional District Demo continued 16 Zoom in and hover over the appropriate congressional district. Notice the total obligations value. Demo continued 17 Review the Response tab for the most recent spending_by_geography API call. Observe that the aggregated_amount value matches the map. *Note that the API responses on USAspending are returned in JSON Demo continued 18 Review the Response tab for the most recent spending_by_geography API call. Observe that the aggregated_amount value matches the map. Demo continued 19 Review the Payload tab for the most recent spending_by_geography API call. Observe that the filters value matches the search filters. Demo continued 20 Review the Payload tab for the most recent spending_by_geography API call. Observe that the filters value matches the search filters. Demo continued 21 Review the Payload tab for the most recent spending_by_geography API call. Observe that the filters value matches the search filters. Demo continued 22 Select the Headers tab and observe the Request URL value. Navigate to the URL and click “Documentation for this endpoint can be found here.” Demo continued 24 Compare the documentation attributes section and the Payload tab. Observe the keys in the payload match the attribute bullets (filters, subawards, scope, etc.). Notice the filters attribute takes an AdvancedFiterObject Demo continued 25 Compare the AdvancedFilterObject documentation and the Advanced Search filter options. AdvancedFilterObject powers advanced search, it is very useful! Demo continued 26 Observe that the time_period filter takes a TimePeriodObject and the recipient_locations filter takes a LocationObject. Demo continued 27 You can use PowerQuery in Excel to import data using POST API requests. In a new Excel workbook select Data > Get Data > From Other Sources > Blank Query Demo continued 28 In the PowerQuery Editor window, select 'Advanced Editor' Demo continued 29 Replace the default code with the code displayed above ) also available on the link below Notes: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/wiki/API-Usage---Power-Query-Example Demo continued 30 PowerQuery handles POST requests in a particular way. For example, lines 1, and 22-24 as well as th e double dou ble -q uotes. Notes: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/wiki/API-Usage---Power-Query-Example Demo continued 31 Compare the code url variable value and the Headers tab Request URL value. Compare the code body va riable value an d the P ayloa d tab Request P aylo ad value. Notes: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/wiki/API-Usage---Power-Query-Example Demo continued 32 Lines 22 – 24 are required to make POST API requests in PowerQuery. Notice the code has no syntax errors. Click Done. Notes: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/wiki/API-Usage---Power-Query-Example Demo continued 33 Observe the query results table and Query Settings panel. Compare the table with the Response tab. Notice that the results record is a List. Click on the List to drill down. Demo continued 34 The List has one item, a Record. Notice the updated APPLIED STEPS in the Query Settings panel. Click the Record to drill down. Demo continued 35 Finally, our data! It should match the Response tab and the map view. Notice the updated applied steps. Click 'Into Table'. Demo continued 36 Once again, notice the updated applied steps. Click 'Advanced Editor' again. Demo continued 37 Notice that the code has been updated to reflect the additional steps. Use this code to automate those steps in the future. Don’t change the added code. Click 'Done'. Demo continued 38 Click 'Close & Load' to load results into a spreadsheet. Additional Exercises How much did my Congressional District receive in COVID-19 funding? COVID-19 Steps: 1. Find this number using the USAspending COVID Exercise profile page. 2. Inspect the page to identify which endpoint is With Steps used to display this number on the webpage. 3. Review the documentation for this endpoint. 4. Use PowerQuery to reproduce this API request in Excel. COVID Profile Page vs Advanced Search DEFC Agencies report transaction-level award data and COVID-19 DEFC award spending data through different systems. USAspending links the award data reported through these different systems to create a more comprehensive picture of government spending. The USAspending Advanced Search tool primarily uses transaction-level award data to filter and present search results. However, since DEFC information is not available at the transaction level, summary stats (in the Time tab, Map tab, and Categories tab) for Advanced Search results with a DEFC filter are an approximation. We built the COVID-19 Spending profile page to present up to date and detailed information on COVID spending. The COVID-19 Spending profile page uses a different set of endpoints compared to Advanced Search. For more information on COVID spending data sources and methodology, please see: https://www.usaspending.gov/disaster/covid-19/data-sources https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/intro-tutorial Demo continued 39 Navigate to the USAspending COVID-19 Spending profile page. Demo continued 40 Scroll down to the Award Spending by Recipient Map. Inspect the page Configure the map: • Area Type: Congressional District • Spending Type: Award Obligations • Amount Type: Total Spending Demo continued 41 The network inspector will only list API requests since you began inspecting the page. Each time you update the map (including zooming) a new API request is made. If you wait to inspect the page until just before you configure the map, it will be easier to find the correct API call. Demo continued 42 Select the most recent spending_by_geography request and open the Request URL in your browser to study the documentation. Demo continued 43 Compare the request payload and documentation attributes. Disaster Spending by Geography Documentation: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending- api/blob/master/usaspending_api/api_contracts/contracts/v2/disaster/spending_by_geography.md The geo_layer_filters attribute takes a list of 4 digit CD FIPS codes. The filter attribute does not take an AdvancedFilterObject, this is different from the Advanced Search endpoints. The filter attribute allows you to filter by DEFC or award type. • You cannot filter by DEFC using the website alone. • The API allows you to accurately answer questions about how much an area received by a particular COVID supplemental appropriation bill. See: https://www.usaspending.gov/disaster/covid-19/data-sources https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/intro-tutorial Demo continued 44 Use this code in PowerQuery to replicate the API call in Excel. This code is available for copy/paste in the link below. Notes: https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/wiki/API-Usage---Power-Query-Example Advanced Search Use Excel to create an API request to replicate an Exercise (On advanced search in USAspending. your own!) Keep learning! Study the list of available endpoints: https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/endpoints Learn more about REST APIs: https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/api/what-is-a-rest-api Learn more about API requests in Python: https://realpython.com/python-requests/

data\\reference\\February_2025_Data_Dict.content: SAM Functional Data Dictionary February 2025 Table of Contents Introduction Change Log Identification This document contains a high-level view of the System for Award Management (SAM) Data Dictionary and directs the reader to various other documents for a more detailed picture of the data elements found within SAM. System Overview The System for Award Management (SAM) integrated the Contract Opportunities, Assistance Listings, Entity Information, Contract Data, Wage Determination, Entity Reporting, Responsibilities and Qualifications, and Federal Hierarchy. Combining these legacy systems streamlined business processes, eliminated data redundancies, and improved regulatory compliance. SAM.gov unifies the government- wide award management systems. If you have the proper roles in SAM, you can register to do business with the U.S. government, update or renew your entity registration, check the status of an entity registration, manage exclusion records, manage user roles, search for entity registrations and exclusion records, and use entity registration and exclusion data. This data dictionary addresses the data elements associated with the business processes required to manage an entity’s Core Data, Assertions, Representations and Certifications, Points of Contact, and the management of Exclusion records. Document Organization This Data Dictionary provides overall listing and descriptions of SAM Entity Management and Exclusion data fields at a high level. Using this document allows you to view the characteristics of data elements and what each is used for. This document includes field definitions and characteristics. The field lengths are the application-limited input lengths. The corresponding extract output lengths may be larger to accommodate migrated data. SAM Field Definitions Field Name: 820s Request Flag Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The flag that indicates whether the entity wants to receive Remittance Advice Notices (820s) through the Value-Added Network (VAN) provider. The user selects “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: ABA Routing Number Type: Numeric Length: 50 Definition: The routing transit number assigned by the American Banker's Association (ABA) for a U.S. financial institution. In SAM, this number must be the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) ABA Routing Number, not the Wire Transfer ABA number. Field Name: Account Number Type: Alphanumeric with Special Characters Length: 20 Definition: The U.S. financial institution account number at which the entity receives EFT payments. Field Name: Account Type Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The entity's financial account type. The user selects “Checking” or “Savings”. Field Name: Accounting Station Type: Alphanumeric Length: 6 Definition: For U.S. government entities, the Accounting Station (Fiscal Station Number) is a six-digit number that identifies the activity which is responsible for performing the official accounting and reporting for the funds. Field Name: ACH Email Type: Alphanumeric Length: 80 Definition: A contact email address for the Automated Clearing House (ACH) Coordinator at the entity’s U.S. financial institution. Field Name: ACH Fax Type: Numeric Length: 30 Definition: The fax number for the ACH Coordinator or Department at the entity’s financial institution. Field Name: ACH Non-U.S. Phone Type: Numeric Length: 30 Definition: The phone number for the ACH Coordinator or Department at the entity’s financial institution if it is located outside of the U.S. Field Name: ACH U.S. Phone Type: Numeric Length: 30 Definition: The phone number for the ACH Coordinator or Department at the entity’s financial institution if it is located in the U.S. Field Name: Active Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the exclusion record became active. This may be different than the date the exclusion record was created. Field Name: Additional Comments Type: Alphanumeric Length: 1,000 Definition: Free-text field where the U.S. government official managing the exclusion record can add additional notes or a description regarding the exclusion. This field can be used for specific agency legislation citations. Field Name: Address Line 1 Type: Alphanumeric Length: 150 Definition: Thefirst line of an address. The following characters are not accepted: ; (Semi Colon) [ (Left square bracket) ] (Right squarebracket) " (Double Quotes) { (Left Curly bracket) } (Right Curly bracket) !(ExclamationPoint) @ (at sign) $ (dollar sign) ˆ (Caret) * (Asterisk) = (Equal sign) Consecutiveinstances of the following characters: .. ++ -- two dashes '' two single quotes Field Name: Address Line 2 Type: Alphanumeric Length: 150 Definition: The second line of an address. The following characters are not accepted: ; (Semi Colon) [ (Left square bracket) ] (Right squarebracket) " (Double Quotes) { (Left Curly bracket) } (Right Curly bracket) !(ExclamationPoint) @ (at sign) $ (dollar sign) ˆ (Caret) * (Asterisk) = (Equal sign) Consecutive instances of the following characters: .. ++ -- two dashes '' two single quotes Field Name: Address Type Type: Alpha Length: 20 Definition: Indicates which address type is captured. Address Type codes include: Field Name: Agency Code Type: Numeric Length: 4 Definition: The U.S. Government Agency identifier aligned to the federal hierarchy. The agency codes were originally sourced from the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS) and the NIST 800-87 listing. Field Name: Agency Location Code Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The Agency Location Code is used to identify accounting reports and documents prepared by or for agency accounting stations and disbursing offices, e.g. eight-digit agency accounting station code, four-digit disbursing office symbol, and three-digit Treasury disbursing center symbol. This eight-digit code corresponds to the registering office. The Agency Location Code is provided by the Treasury IPAC system. The user selects from a list of ALCs populated based on the Department Code selected. Field Name: Agency Parent Type: Alpha Length: 10 Definition: The name of the immediate parent of the excluding agency. This may be used to determine the Department under which the exclusion record falls. Field Name: Architect-Engineer Responses Type: N/A Length: N/A Definition: The Architect and Engineering Responses provided during the Representations & Certifications part of an entity registration are used to complete the Standard Form (SF) 330 Part II for architect-engineer contracts. A-E Responses only apply to entities who selected one or more of the relevant NAICS Codes (541310, 541320, 541330, 541360, 541370,541410, and 541620). The elements associated with these responses are detailed in the Full User Guides found within SAM Help (Federal User Guide Section 4.5.3 and Non-Federal User Guide Section 4.4.3). Field Name: Attachment Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The pre- signed URL to access the attachment in R/Q page under Other Responsibility and Integrity Information. Field Name: Authorization Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The effective date of an entity's EFT account authorization. The Authorization Date will be pre-filled by the system as the date a registration was created/updated. The Authorization Date must be present if an ABA Routing Number/financial institute was entered. Field Name: Average Annual Receipts Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: The average yearly receipts for the past five years for the location being registered rounded to the nearest dollar. This number must be less than or equal to the Total Receipts number. Field Name: Average Number of Employees Type: Numeric Length: 25 Definition: The number of worldwide employees for all affiliate, branches, etc. for an entity. Its value must be equal to or greater than the Location Number of Employees. Users must enter a value of 0 or greater. Field Name: Barrels Capacity Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: The number of Barrels per Day of Petroleum Refining if the entity selected NAICS Code 324110 as one of its NAICS offerings. This number will be compared against the SBA's small business size standard table to determine whether the company meets the small business concern threshold for this NAICS. Field Name: Bonding Level Type Type: Multi-Select Length: N/A Definition: The type of bonding level selected by an entity including their registration on the Disaster Response Registry. Possible values for this field are: Field Name: Bonding Level Value Type: Numeric Length: 22 Definition: The dollar value (per contract or aggregate) of a Service or Construction Bond. This is used in the Disaster Response Registry. Field Name: Bonding to Bid Flag Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The flag that determines whether the entity requires bonding to bid on contracts. User selects “Yes” or “No”. This is used in the Disaster Response Registry. Field Name: Entity Start Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the entity was started or acquired. The format is MM/DD/YYYY (example: 01/01/1995) and must be today's date or earlier. Field Name: Business Types Type: Alphanumeric Length: 2 Definition: The different business types that can classify an entity. Some are set by external parties. Most are self-selected by the registrant. The following business type is set or reset by the AbilityOne Program and cannot be selected by the registrant directly: If the entity is a government agency, one of the following business types must be selected: The remainder of the business types can be self-selected by the registrant: Field Name: CAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code is a five-character alpha- numeric identifier assigned to entities located in the United States and its outlying areas by the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Program to identify a given facility or location of a commercial or government entity. Some registrations in SAM go through the CAGE Code assignment/validation process after submission, dependent on Purpose of Registration and other factors. Field Name: City Type: Alpha Length: 40 Definition: The name of the city in a given address type. The following characters are not accepted: ; (Semi Colon) [ (Left square bracket) ] (Right squarebracket) " (Double Quotes) { (Left Curly bracket) } (Right Curly bracket) !(ExclamationPoint) @ (at sign) $ (dollar sign) ˆ (Caret) * (Asterisk) = (Equal sign) Consecutive instances of the following characters: .. ++ -- two dashes '' two single quotes Field Name: Classification Type Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: Identifies the type of party that has been excluded. Individual is a person without a valid UEI. Firm is a company or organization with a valid UEI (includes sole proprietors who have obtained a UEI). Special Entity Designation is an organization or thing capable of bearing legal rights and responsibilities which does not have a UEI and is not an individual, firm, or vessel. Vessel is a mode of transportation capable of transport by water. Field Name: Entity Division Name Type: Alpha Length: 60 Definition: The Division Name, if the entity registering does business as a division or is part of a larger company, as provided by the entity in Core Data. Field Name: Entity Division Number Type: Numeric Length: 10 Definition: The Division Number, if the entity registering is identified by a number within their organization, as provided by the entity in Core Data. Field Name: Company Security Level Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The facility security level for the entity registering as provided in Core Data. Possible Values for this field are: Field Name: Completion Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the contract was signed for which a BioPreferred Report is being submitted. This value is pre-populated from the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS). Field Name: Congressional District Type: Numeric Length: 10 Definition: The Congressional District of an entity located in the U.S. or its outlying areas as calculated by the system based on the entity’s physical address. While the Entity Congressional District is usually displayed as 2 characters, there may be instances where this can be updated to have STATE + 2-digit Entity Congressional District, for a total of 10 characters. Field Name: Contracting Agency Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The specified federal agency for which the entity submitting a BioPreferred Report is providing services/products. This value is pre-populated from FPDS. Field Name: Contracting Department Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The specified federal department for which the entity submitting a BioPreferred Report is providing services/products. This value is pre-populated from FPDS. Field Name: Contract Sign Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the Biopreferred Report Contract was signed. This value is pre-populated from FPDS. Field Name: Entity URL Type: 200 Length: Alphanumeric Definition: The entity's website Universal Resource Locator (URL) as provided by the entity in Core Data. Field Name: Correspondence Flag Type: Alpha Length: 1 Definition: A field used by the predecessor system to SAM, this data is not collected in SAM and would only appear in records migrated from the Central Contractor Registration (CCR) database. This field was used to identify an entity's preferred correspondence type. Possible values for this field are: Field Name: Country Code Type: Alpha Length: 3 Definition: The country code representing where the entity is located. Codes adhere to the U.S. Government’s Geographic Entity Name and Code (GENC) Profile of the ISO 3166 International Standard for country codes. SAM can also accommodate two-character country codes. Field Name: Country of Incorporation Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The country code representing where the entity was incorporated. Codes adhere to the U.S. Government’s Geographic Entity Name and Code (GENC) Profile of the ISO 3166 International Standard for country codes. SAM can also accommodate two-character country codes. Users select from a pre-defined list of countries. Field Name: Credit Card Usage Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The field which indicates whether an entity is willing to be paid by Government credit card. User selects “Yes” to indicate that they will and “No” to indicate they will not. Field Name: Cross Reference Type: Alpha Length: 15 Definition: Method for identifying linkage among exclusion records. Types of cross references include: Field Name: DBA Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The 'Doing Business As' name of the entity. This name must be different from the Legal Business Name. This field cannot be changed in SAM. It is part of the entity’s record as validated through SAM’s Entity Validation Service provider. Field Name: Debt Subject to Offset Flag Type: Alpha Length: 1 Definition: The indicator which shows whether the United States Treasury's Debt Management Services notified SAM that the entity represented by this UEI has a delinquent debt subject to collection under the Treasury Offset Program. Contracting officers may not use the governmentwide commercial purchase card to pay this entity for contracts/orders above the micro-purchase threshold as outlined in FAR 32.1108(b)(2). This flag set to Yes (Y) indicates that the registrant has been determined to have a delinquent obligation owed to the U. S. Federal Government as shown by records at the Department of the Treasury. No (N) means the Treasury Department found no delinquent obligation. A non-entry [-] indicates that this registrant has not yet been verified with Treasury. Foreign registrations are not verified. Field Name: Department Codes Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The two-character Department or Independent Agency code currently derived from the Treasury Index. The user selects from a pre-defined list. Field Name: Description of Requirement Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4000 Definition: The description of services and construction contract actions as entered in FPDS for contracts subject to BioPreferred reporting. Field Name: DFARS Response Type: N/A Length: N/A Definition: The entity's responses to DFARS related questions provided during the Representations & Certifications part of the registration. Field Name: Disaster Response Flag Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The indicator which shows the entity provided Disaster Response Information to be part of the Disaster Response Registry. Contractors on the Disaster Response Registry are willing to provide debris removal, distribution of supplies, reconstruction, and other disaster or emergency relief supplies and/or services. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Disbursing Office Symbol Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The unique symbol assigned by the Treasury Intra-governmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) system for the office disbursing funds. The disbursing office has a relationship to the agency location code. Users select from a pre-defined list of values. Field Name: Disposition Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The short description of the proceeding disposition selected from a drop-down list entered by the entity if they report Proceeding Details in Core Data. The possible values for this field are either Conviction/Finding of Fault or Other acknowledgment of fault. Field Name: DoDAAC Type: Alphanumeric Length: 9 Definition: The Department of Defense Activity Address Code (DoDAAC) for non-civilian government entities (DoD). This is filled with the letters "DOD" followed by the entity’s six-digit assigned DoDAAC. Field Name: DoDAAC Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The legal business name of the DoD entity associated with the DoDAAC record. Field Name: Dollar Amount Spent Type: Numeric Length: 20 Definition: The entity-reported Dollar Amount expended in any given BioPreferred product category during the Federal Government fiscal year (October 1 – September 30). Field Name: Entity EFT Indicator Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4 Definition: The Entity EFT Indicator is an entity-selected Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Identifier used to distinguish more than one remittance location for payment. An entity can only provide an Entity EFT Indicator if they provide an additional set of EFT information. If the entity does not need to provide additional EFT information, the registration will show a value of null. CAGE Codes are assigned at the Entity EFT Indicator level. Field Name: EDI (Y/N) Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This is the flag that determines whether the entity wants to enter Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) Information in the Assertions section of the entity registration. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: EDI VAN Provider Type: Alphanumeric Length: 20 Definition: The Value-Added Network (VAN) Provider supporting the entity’s EDI exchange. Field Name: EFT Waiver Type: Alpha Length: 1 Definition: The EFT Waiver Flag indicates whether EFT information for a U.S. financial institution is required for the entity. Values are Y for Yes and N for No. Field Name: Email Type: Alphanumeric Length: 80 Definition: The email address for the entity-provided point of contact. Field Name: Entity Structure Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The structure of the entity as defined by the IRS. Users select from a pre-defined list. Possible values for this field are: Field Name: EVS Monitoring Address Line 1 Type: Alphanumeric Length: 150 Definition: The first line of the address as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Address Line 2 Type: Alphanumeric Length: 150 Definition: The second line of the address as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring City Type: Alpha Length: 35 Definition: The name of the city in which the entity is located as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 130 Definition: The legal business name provided for the entity by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Country Code Type: Numeric Length: 3 Definition: The country code in which the entity is located as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring DBA Type: Alpha Length: 120 Definition: The Doing Business As (DBA) name of the entity provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Last Updated Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the EVS monitoring service was last updated for the entity. Field Name: EVS Monitoring State or Province Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The state or province code in which the entity is located as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Status Type: Numeric Length: 1 Definition: The indicator which shows whether EVS monitoring is turned on for the entity. Values are 0 for No and 1 for Yes. Field Name: EVS Monitoring Zip Code/ Postal Code Type: Numeric Length: 10 Definition: The U.S. ZIP Code, or international Postal Code, associated with the address as provided by the EVS monitoring service. Field Name: EVS Out of Business Indicator Type: Numeric Length: 1 Definition: The status code which indicates EVS has information the entity is either out of business or has had a period of inactivity uncharacteristic to the industry. Values are 0 for No and 1 for Yes. Field Name: Excluding Agency Type: Alpha Length: 120 Definition: The name of the federal agency which created and manages the exclusion record. Field Name: Exclusion Program Type: Alpha Length: 15 Definition: The program in which an exclusion record is classified. New records will automatically default to Reciprocal. Field Name: Exclusion Status Flag Type: Alpha Length: 1 Definition: This flag indicates whether an entity, as identified by the UEI registered, has an exclusion record. If this flag is set to Yes, the registrant has an exclusion record. A value of No indicates this registrant's UEI does not have an exclusion record in SAM. Values are N for No and Y for Yes. Field Name: Exclusion Type Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: One of four categories under which an exclusion is created. Each Exclusion Type has standard language for the Nature (Cause) and Effect. Users should read the language carefully to understand the impact of the exclusion. Field Name: Executive Compensation Question 1 Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a "yes" or "no" response to the first Executive Compensation screening question which reads, “In your business or organization's preceding completed fiscal year, did your business or organization (the legal entity to which this specific SAM record, represented by a UEI, belongs) receive both of the following: 1. 80 percent or more of your annual gross revenue in U.S. federal contracts, subcontracts, loans, grants, subgrants, and/or cooperative agreements, and 2. $25,000,000 or more in annual gross revenues from U.S. federal contracts, subcontracts, loans, grants, subgrants, and/or cooperative agreements?” Users select “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Executive Compensation Question 2 Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a "yes" or "no" response to the second Executive Compensation screening question which is conditional based upon the entity’s response to the first question. The second question reads “Does the public have access to information about the compensation of the senior executives in your business or organization (the legal entity to which this specific SAM record, represented by a UEI, belongs) through periodic reports filed under section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m(a), 780(d)) or section 6104 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986?” Users select “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Executive First Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 65 Definition: The first name of one of the five most highly compensated executives in a registered entity including parent organizations, all branches, and all affiliates worldwide. Executives are considered officers, managing partners, or any other employees in management positions. Field Name: Executive Middle Initial Type: Alphanumeric Length: 3 Definition: The middle initial of one of the five most highly compensated executives in a registered entity including parent organizations, all branches, and all affiliates worldwide. Executives are considered officers, managing partners, or any other employees in management positions. Field Name: Executive Last Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 65 Definition: The last name of one of the five most highly compensated executives in a registered entity including parent organizations, all branches, and all affiliates worldwide. Executives are considered officers, managing partners, or any other employees in management positions. Field Name: Executive Title Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The position title of one of the five most highly compensated executives in a registered entity including parent organizations, all branches, and all affiliates worldwide. Executives are considered officers, managing partners, or any other employees in management positions. Field Name: Registration Expiration Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: A system-generated date representing when an entity's registration expires. The expiration date will automatically update when the registration, or changes made to the registration, become active. The expiration date is set 365 days from when the user submits an update to their entity’s information, except for updates only made to points of contact (POC Only) which do not reset the expiration date. If the registrant has not updated their Entity Management information at least once in the past 365 days, the registration becomes inactive. Field Name: Extension Type: Numeric Length: 16 Definition: The phone number extension of the Point of Contact (POC) within an entity management registration if they are located in the U.S. Field Name: FASCSA Order Flag Type: Alphanumeric Length: 1 Definition: Identifies an Exclusion as a FASCSA Order Field Name: FAR Response Type: N/A Length: N/A Definition: The entity's responses to FAR-related questions provided during the Representations & Certifications part of the registration. Field Name: Fax Type: Numeric Length: 30 Definition: The fax number for the Point of Contact (POC) within an entity management registration. Field Name: Financial Assistance Certifications Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator which shows if the entity wishes to apply for a Federal financial assistance project or program, or if the entity is currently the recipient of funding under any Federal financial assistance project or program. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Financial Institute Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The name of an entity's bank or other financial institution. This name is tied to the ABA routing number and will be pre-populated after the ABA routing number is entered. Field Name: First Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 65 Definition: The first name for the Point of Contact (POC) within an entity management registration. Field Name: Fiscal Year End Close Date Type: Date Length: 4 Definition: The date the entity's accounting period closes. When entering the information on the web site, you must enter as MM/DD. Field Name: Foreign Province Type: Alpha Length: 55 Description: The foreign province in which the POC is located. This field is mandatory only for Canadian addresses. Field Name: Functional Group Identifier Type: Alphanumeric Length: 15 Definition: The Functional Group (GS02) Identifier for those entities providing EDI information in the Assertions section of the registration. Field Name: Geographic Area Served: County Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The code for the county within a state used to designate an area served in the Disaster Response Registry. Users select from a pre-defined list based on the State selected. Field Name: Geographic Area Served: Metropolitan Statistical Area Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The name of the Metropolitan Statistical Area that may span county or state borders and is used in the Disaster Response Registry to designate an area served. Users select from a pre- defined list based on the State and County selected. Field Name: Geographic Area Served: State Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The state selected by an entity when designating an area served in the Disaster Response Registry. Field Name: Geographic Area Served: Type Type: Alpha Length: 3 Definition: The name of the type of geographic area served for the Disaster Response Registry. The possible values for this field are: Field Name: Highest Employee Security Level Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The top level of security clearance for employees in an entity. Possible Values for this field are: Field Name: Highest Level Owner Status Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator which shows if the entity stated it is has an Immediate Owner which is owned or controlled by another entity in accordance with the FAR Subpart 4.18 definitions. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Highest Level Owner Location Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator showing if the Highest-Level Owner is not located in the U.S. and its outlying areas. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Highest Level Owner CAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The CAGE Code selected by the entity which represents their Highest-Level Owner located in the U.S. and its outlying areas. Field Name: Highest Level Owner NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The NCAGE Code selected by the entity which represents their Highest-Level Owner located outside U.S. and its outlying areas. Field Name: Highest Owner Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: Legal Business Name of Highest Owner Field Name: Immediate Owner Status Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator which shows if the entity stated it has an Owner in accordance with the FAR Subpart 4.18 definitions. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Immediate Owner Location Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator showing if the Immediate Owner is in the U.S. and its outlying areas. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Immediate Owner CAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The CAGE Code selected by the entity which represents their Immediate Owner located in the side U.S. and its outlying areas. Field Name: Immediate Owner NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The NCAGE Code selected by the entity which represents their Immediate Owner not located in the side U.S. and its outlying areas. Field Name: Indefinite Indicator Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a Yes or No response to indicate if an exclusion record is marked as Indefinite, i.e. no termination date is set. Field Name: Individual First Name Type: Alpha Length: 65 Definition: The first name of an individual with an exclusion record. Field Name: Individual Last Name Type: Alpha Length: 65 Definition: The last name of an individual with an exclusion record. Field Name: Individual Middle Name Type: Alpha Length: 50 Definition: The middle name of an individual with an exclusion record. Field Name: Individual Prefix Type: Alpha Length: 25 Definition: The prefix of an individual with an exclusion record. Field Name: Individual Suffix Type: Alpha Length: 25 Definition: The suffix of an individual with an exclusion record. Field Name: Initial Registration Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the entity initially registered to do businesses with the U.S. government entity registration was submitted. This date can precede the SAM go-live date of July 2012 if the entity was registered in the prior Central Contractor Registration system. This date will not change. Field Name: Instrument Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The type of proceedings instrument entered by the entity in the proceeding details. The values are U.S. Federal issued contract, U.S. Federal issued grant / assistance instrument, State issued contract, and State issued grant. Field Name: Instrument Number Type: Numeric Length: 50 Definition: The official number of the proceeding as assigned by proceedings instrument. Field Name: ISA Identifier Type: Alphanumeric Length: 15 Definition: The Interchange Sender (ISA) Identifier specific to Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) information. It cannot be longer than fifteen characters. It is an alphanumeric value that does not include dashes, spaces, or special characters. Field Name: ISA Qualifier Type: Alphanumeric Length: 2 Definition: The Interchange Sender (ISA) Qualifier specific to Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) information. Field Name: Last Name Type: Alpha Length: 65 Definition: The last name of the Point of Contact within an entity management registration. Field Name: Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The Legal Business Name of the entity as validated by EVS. Note: It cannot contain the following special characters: "", å, å, ø, Å This field cannot be changed in SAM. Field Name: Location Employees Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: The one-year average number of employees at the location being registered. This is an optional field, but if completed, must be less than or equal to the Worldwide Number of Employees provided in Goods and Services. Field Name: Lockbox Number Type: Numeric Length: 20 Definition: The lockbox number assigned by the entity’s financial institution if the one is used by the entity to receive payment. Field Name: Megawatt Hours Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: The number showing total Megawatt Hours (MWH) for the preceding fiscal year of all affiliates of an entity registrant using one of the following NAICS codes: 221111, 221112, 221113, 221121, 221122. This value is used to calculate the Small Business size status by industry. Field Name: Merchant ID 1 Type: Numeric Length: 130 Definition: The number assigned to an entity by the bank that processes their credit card receipts. The Merchant ID Number is similar to a routing number. This field is for Government Use Only. Field Name: Merchant ID 2 Type: Numeric Length: 130 Definition: This is an alternate ID to Merchant ID 1 and is used if the registering entity has two routing numbers (uses both banks). This field is for Government Use Only. Field Name: Middle Initial Type: Alpha Length: 3 Definition: The middle initial of the Point of Contact within an entity management registration. Field Name: Modification Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date received from FPDS representing the last date the contract was modified for the Total Contract Value. Field Name: Modification Number Type: Alphanumeric Length: 25 Definition: The placeholder number received from FPDS to signify the amount of times the contract was modified. Field Name: NAICS Code Type: Numeric Length: 6 Definition: The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code(s). Effective January 1, 2022, SAM uses the 2022 revision of the NAICS. Field Name: NAICS Exception Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4 Definition: The associated NAICS size standard exception data from the Small Business Administration (SBA). This includes the NAICS exception number and description. Field Name: Name of Individual Executing Consent Type: Alpha Length: 60 Definition: The name of the individual providing the authorization for the entity Taxpayer Name and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to be sent to the IRS for validation. This person must have legal authority to execute this consent in accordance with 26 CFR section 301.6103(c)- 1(e)(4). For example, if the taxpayer is a legal entity, such as a corporation, any officer of the entity with authority under applicable State law to legally bind the entity may execute a consent to disclosure. Field Name: NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: CAGE Codes for foreign entities used internationally as part of the NATO Codification System (NCS) are called NCAGE Codes. NCAGE Codes are assigned by a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) or by the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). DLA’s CAGE Program records and maintains NCAGE Codes in the CAGE master file. All entities not located in the U.S. and its outlying areas must provide an NCAGE Code when they register. Field Name: Non-US Phone Type: Numeric Length: 30 Definition: The phone number of the Point of Contact for an entity management registration if they are located outside of the U.S. Field Name: No Public Display Flag Type: Checkbox Length: N/A Definition: The field indicates whether an entity has chosen to opt-out of their registration being displayed in SAM public search results. Opting out may result in a reduction in Federal Government business opportunities, and subcontractors who choose this option will not be visible to prime contractors. Entities that have opted out will be removed only from the SAM public search but will still be visible to users with For Official Use Only (FOUO) data access and will be provided in accordance with Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests. Field Name: NPI Type: Numeric Length: 10 Definition: The NPI (National Provider Identifier) is a unique identification number for covered health care providers. It is an optional field for exclusion records. Field Name: Organization Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 200 Definition: The name of an excluded entity that falls under one of the following Classification Types: Special Entity Designation or Vessel. Field Name: PIID Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The Procurement Instrument Identifier (PIID) is used to identify solicitation and contract actions in designated support and reporting systems (e.g., Federal Procurement Data System), in accordance with regulations, applicable authorities, and agency policies and procedures. Field Name: Place of Performance City Type: Alphanumeric Length: 100 Definition: City where the BioPreferred report is detailing USDA information. Field Name: Place of Performance Country Type: Alphanumeric Length: 100 Definition: Country where the BioPreferred report is detailing USDA information. Field Name: Place of Performance County Type: Alphanumeric Length: 100 Definition: County where the BioPreferred report is detailing USDA information. Field Name: Place of Performance State/Province Type: Alphanumeric Length: 2 Definition: State or Province where the BioPreferred report is detailing USDA information. Field Name: Place of Performance ZIP Type: Alphanumeric Length: 10 Definition: U.S. ZIP Code, or international Postal Code, associated with the Place of Performance address pre-populated by the system in a BioPreferred Report. Field Name: POC Notes Type: Alpha Length: 1000 Definition: Additional notes or comments of a Point of Contact for an entity management registration. Field Name: POC Title Type: Alpha Length: 50 Definition: The title of the Point of Contact for an entity management registration. Field Name: POC Type Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The type of Point of Contact identified for an entity management registration. Users select from a pre-defined list of values based on the entity type. Possible values for this field are: Field Name: Predecessor Details Status Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The indicator which shows if the entity stated it is a successor to a predecessor that held a Federal contract or grant within the last three years. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Predecessor 1 CAGE Code or NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The CAGE Code or NCAGE Code for the most recent predecessor reported by the entity. Field Name: Predecessor 2 CAGE Code or NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The CAGE Code or NCAGE Code for the second most recent predecessor reported by the entity. Field Name: Predecessor 3 CAGE Code or NCAGE Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 5 Definition: The CAGE Code or NCAGE Code for the third most recent predecessor reported by the entity. Field Name: Predecessor Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: Legal Business Name Prior to Entity Field Name: Previous Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The previous legal business name of the entity as supplied by EVS. Field Name: Primary NAICS Type: Alphanumeric Length: 1 Definition: The indicator showing the NAICS Code selected by the entity as their primary NAICS. For many programs, SBA requires a firm be “small” in its primary industry in accordance with SBA’s size standards for that industry. Field Name: Prior UEI Type: Alphanumeric Length: 12 Definition: Any prior UEI (Unique Entity Identifier) for an entity. Field Name: Proceeding Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date of the entity's proceeding. Field Name: Proceeding Description Type: Alpha Length: 4000 Definition: A description of the proceeding entered by the user. Field Name: Proceeding Question 1 Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a "yes" or "no" response to the first Proceedings Screening question which reads, “Is there a Federal solicitation on which your business or organization, as represented by the UEI on this specific SAM record, is bidding that contains the FAR provision 52.209-7, or has your business or organization, as represented by the UEI on this specific SAM record, been awarded a Federal contract or assistance award that contains the award term and condition described in 2 C.F.R. 200 Appendix XII?” Users select “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Proceeding Question 2 Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a "yes" or "no" response to the second Proceedings Screening question which reads, “Does your business or organization, as represented by the UEI on this specific SAM record, have current active Federal contracts and/or grants with total value (including any exercised/unexercised options) greater than $10,000,000?” Users select “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Proceeding Question 3 Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This field will store a "yes" or "no" response to the third Proceedings Screening question which reads, “Within the last five years, has the business or organization, as represented by the UEI on this specific SAM record, and/or any of its principles, in connection with the award to or performance by the business or organization of a Federal contract or grant, been the subject of a Federal or State: 1. Criminal proceeding resulting in a conviction or other acknowledgement of fault; 2. Civil proceeding resulting in a find of fault with a monetary fine, penalty, reimbursement, restitution, and/or damages greater than $5,000, or other acknowledgement of fault; and/or 3. Administrative proceeding resulting in a finding of fault with either a monetary fine or penalty greater than $5,000 or reimbursement, restitution, or damages greater than $100,000, or another acknowledgement of fault?” Users select “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: Proceeding State Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The state where the entity's reported proceeding occurred. Field Name: Proceeding Type Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: This is the type of proceeding. Users select from a pre-defined list of values. The possible values for this field are: Field Name: Procurement or Federal Assistance ID Type: Alphanumerical Length: 50 Definition: This field describes whether the records have Contract Data ID or a Grant ID Field Name: Product Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4000 Definition: A description of the specific product used under the USDA category for BioPreferred reporting. Field Name: Province Type: Alpha Length: 50 Definition: The province in which a non-U.S. entity is located. Field Name: PSC Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: The descriptive short name for the selected Product Service Code (PSC). Field Name: PSC Code Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4 Definition: The four-position code used to describe products, services, and research and development (R&D) the entity is offering to the federal government. Products have a digit in the first position. Services and R&D have a character in the first position. An entity can select up to 500 PSCs to include in their entity registration. Field Name: PSC Description Type: Alphanumeric Length: 4000 Definition: The long description of the type of products or services being used. Field Name: Reason for Modification Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: A summary of why the modification of the BioPreferred report was made which results in changes in Total Contract Value or funding information. Field Name: Record Date Type: Text Length: 55 Definition: The effective date of termination. Field Name: Record Type Type: Text Length: 1 Definition: The one-character code that references the record type for Termination (e.g., ‘A’) Field Name: RecordTypeDesc Type: Text Length: 55 Definition: The descriptive text that matches the recordType code (e.g., Administrative Agreement) Field Name: Reference PIID Type: Alphanumeric Length: 50 Definition: When reporting orders under Indefinite Delivery Vehicles (IDV) such as a GWAC, IDC, FSS, BOA, or BPA, report the Procurement Instrument Identifier (Contract Number or Agreement Number) of the IDV. Field Name: Purpose of Registration Type: Radio Button Length: N/A Definition: The purpose of an entity’s registration in SAM as determined by the user’s response to the following question: “Why are you registering this entity to do business with the U.S. government?” The possible values for this field are: Field Name: Registration Status Type: Alpha Length: 1 Definition: This field tracks the registration status of the entity. The possible values are: Field Name: Remittance Name Type: Alpha Length: 120 Definition: The name of the party to whom the check should be made payable if the government is unable to pay using EFT. Field Name: Renewal Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date that the entity renewed their registration. Field Name: SBA Certification Entry Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date an entity received its SBA certification as provided by SBA. Field Name: SBA Certification Exit Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date an entity exited the SBA certification program as provided by SBA. Field Name: Search More Locations Question Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: Federal users indicate whether they want to search for more locations related to the Firm exclusion they are creating. Users select either “Yes” or “No”. Field Name: State/ Province Type: Alpha Length: 2 Definition: The state/ province code in which the U.S. entity is located. Field Name: State of Incorporation Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The state where the entity was incorporated. Only required for U.S. incorporated entities. Field Name: Tax Year Type: Numeric Length: 4 Definition: The most recent Tax Year in which the entity reported taxes as provided by the entity on the IRS Consent page. It must be no later than the current calendar year. Field Name: Taxpayer Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The Taxpayer Name the IRS has on file for the entity's TIN according to its most recent tax return. The Taxpayer Name may be slightly different than the Legal Business Name of the entity being registered. The Taxpayer Name can only contain letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens (-), and ampersands (&). Field Name: Termination Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date the exclusion record will be removed from the active list of exclusions and become inactive. A user may indicate a date that occurred in the past to immediately make an exclusion inactive. Field Name: Tax Identification Number Type: Numeric Length: 9 Definition: The Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for an entity, which can be either the Employer Identification Number (EIN) or the Social Security Number (SSN) if the entity is a Sole Proprietor or a Single-Member Limited Liability Company (LLC). Field Name: TIN Consent Date Type: Date Length: 8 Definition: The date that an individual provided authorization for the entity Taxpayer Name and TIN to be sent to the IRS for validation. Field Name: TIN Consent Signature Type: Alphanumeric Length: 9 Definition: The signature of the individual who authorized the entity information to be sent to the IRS for validation. Field Name: Title of Individual Executing Consent Type: Alphanumeric Length: 60 Definition: The title of the individual providing the authorization for the entity Taxpayer Name and TIN to be sent to the IRS for validation. This person must have legal authority to execute this consent in accordance with 26 CFR section 301.6103(c)-1(e) (4). For example, if the taxpayer is a legal entity, such as a corporation, any officer of the entity with authority under applicable State law to legally bind the entity may execute consent to disclosure. Field Name: Total Assets Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: An entity’s total assets. This number is used in the small business size status calculation for NAICS Codes 522110, 522120, 522130, 522190, 522210, and 522293 in accordance with the SBA Table of Small Business Size Standards. Field Name: Total Compensation Amount Type: Numeric Length: 38 Definition: The dollar value for the total compensation of the executive named in the Executive Name field. Field Name: Total Contract Value Type: Numeric Length: 20 Definition: The total amount of procurement that was obligated to be spent on products or services for the place of performance. Field Name: Total Receipts Type: Numeric Length: 15 Definition: The average yearly receipts for an entity over the past five years for all worldwide affiliates, branches, etc. rounded to the nearest dollar. This number must be equal to or greater than the Location Annual Receipts number. Field Name: Type of Contract Type: Alphanumeric Length: 120 Definition: The type of contract determines the service contract reporting thresholds in accordance with FAR Subpart 4.17 Service Contract Inventory. Field Name: Type of Tax Type: Alpha Length: 22 Definition: The type of tax paid to IRS. This will be prefilled by the system to say: Applicable Federal Tax. Field Name: Ultimate Parent UEI Type: Alphanumeric Length: 12 Definition: The UEI of the ultimate parent entity of the registrant, i.e. the very highest level of the organizational structure. Value provided by EVS. Field Name: Ultimate Parent Legal Business Name Type: Alphanumeric Length: 150 Definition: The legal business name of the ultimate parent entity of the registrant. Value provided by EVS. Field Name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Type: Alphanumeric Length: 12 Definition: The unique, twelve-character entity identifier in SAM. Field Name: USDA Category Type: Drop-Down Length: N/A Definition: The USDA biobased product categories for the Federal Procurement Preference: Field Name: US Phone Type: Numeric Length: 13 Definition: The phone number of the Point of Contact for an entity registration if they are in the U.S. Field Name: Vessel Call Sign Type: Alphanumeric Length: 8 Definition: A vessel’s unique identification code as used in radio communication. Mostly found on Firm exclusion records, but could be in other types if the 15 CAGE 5 Individual, Special Entity, or Vessel has a CAGE Code. 16 Excluding Agency Identifies the Agency which created the exclusion. 25 This field provides the Agency creating the exclusion space to enter 17 Additional Comments additional information as necessary. N/A Identifies the date the exclusion went active. 18 Active Date Format: MM/DD/YYYY 10 SAM Exclusions Public V2 FASCSA Orders Extract Layout December 1, 2023 1 Identifies the date the exclusion will be terminated. data\\reference\\Lookup-Tables\\conflict.content: UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset Codebook Version 19.1 Uppsala Conflict Data Program Department of Peace and Conflict Research Uppsala University Centre for the Study of Civil Wars International Peace Research Institute, Oslo This version compiled and updated by Therese Pettersson (2019) When using this data, please always cite: Gleditsch, Nils Petter; Peter Wallensteen, Mikael Eriksson, Margareta Sollenberg & Håvard Strand (2002) Armed Conflict 1946–2001: A New Dataset. Journal of Peace Research 39(5): 615–637. Pettersson, Therese; Stina Högbladh & Magnus Öberg (2019). Organized violence, 1989-2018 and peace agreements. Journal of Peace Research 56(4). When appropriate, also cite this codebook: Pettersson, Therese (2019) UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset Codebook v 19.1 (https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/). Always include the Version number in analyses using the dataset. When referring to the dataset, make sure to use the correct name: the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset. Contents 1 Introduction .................................................................................................................................... 3 2 Definition of armed conflict ........................................................................................................... 1 2.1 State-based Armed Conflict................................................................................................... 1 3 Variables in the Armed Conflict Dataset ...................................................................................... 3 4 Additional information on variables in the dataset ....................................................................... 7 4.1 Location .................................................................................................................................. 7 4.2 Incompatibility ........................................................................................................................ 8 4.3 Start dates temporal precision ............................................................................................... 8 4.4 Episode end dates temporal precision .................................................................................. 9 4.5 System Membership Description ........................................................................................... 9 5 Missing data .................................................................................................................................. 11 6 Version Name Convention .......................................................................................................... 11 7 References .................................................................................................................................... 12 Appendix 1 List of System Members Since 1946 ............................................................................... 13 1 Introduction This document describes the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset, a joint project between the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) at the Department of Peace and Conflict Research, Uppsala University and the Centre for the Study of Civil War at the International Peace Research Institute in Oslo (PRIO). The first release of the Armed Conflict Dataset was prepared at PRIO in 2002 in close collaboration with researchers at UCDP and the Departments of Sociology and Political Science and Geomatics at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU). For a description of the division of labor in creating the database, see the first footnote in the article presenting the dataset, Gleditsch et al. (2002: 615). This footnote also lists the financial sources of support for the entire project and credits for comments and advice received along the way. The dataset is available for download from http://www.pcr.uu.se/research/ucdp/datasets/. Both UCDP and PRIO offer a range of other datasets, compatible with the UCDP/PRIO dataset. Of special importance is the UCDP Dyadic dataset, which is based on the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset, but goes beneath the conflict level and focuses on different dyads within each conflict. Further compatible datasets can be found on both PRIO’s and UCDP’s web pages. This is version 19.1 of the codebook and associated documents. For our policy on version labeling, see Section 6 below, and for a complete history of earlier versions see the document called Version History. For further comments and suggestions on the data and the codebook, please communicate both to ucdp@pcr.uu.se and to jpr@prio.no. Earlier versions and definitions: Lotta Themnér Peter Wallensteen Birger Heldt Margareta Sollenberg Mikael Eriksson & Stina Högbladh Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) Håvard Strand Håvard M. Nygård Halvard Buhaug Joachim Carlsen Nils Petter Gleditsch Håvard Hegre Christin M. Ormhaug & Lars Wilhelmsen International Peace Research Institute, Oslo (PRIO) 2 Definition of armed conflict The main unit in this dataset is a “State-based Armed Conflict” as defined by UCDP.1 This definition is presented unabridged in Section 2.1. Each conflict is listed in the database and given a unique ID code. The temporal aspect of a conflict is not addressed by this definition; hence, two conflict episodes over the same incompatibility will be assigned the same ID regardless of the time separating them. See below for further clarifications. 2.1 State-based Armed Conflict UCDP defines state-based armed conflict as: “a contested incompatibility that concerns government and/or territory where the use of armed force between two parties, of which at least one is the government of a state, results in at least 25 battle-related deaths in a calendar year.” The separate elements of the definition are operationalized as follows: (1) Use of armed force: use of arms, resulting in deaths. (1.1) Arms: any material means, e.g. manufactured weapons but also sticks, stones, fire, water etc. (2) 25 deaths: A minimum of 25 battle-related deaths per year and per dyad (see Item 3.3 in this definition) in an incompatibility.2 (3) Party: A government of a state or any opposition organization or alliance of organizations. UCDP distinguishes between primary and secondary parties. Primary parties are those that form an incompatibility by stating incompatible positions (see Item 5 in this definition). At least one of the primary parties is the government of a state. Secondary parties are states that enter a conflict with troops to actively support one of the primary parties. The secondary party must share the position of the primary party it is supporting in the incompatibility. (3.1) Government: The party controlling the capital of a state. (3.2) Opposition organization: Any non-governmental group of people having announced a name for their group and using armed force to influence the outcome of the stated incompatibility (see Item 5 in this definition). The UCDP only deals with formally organized opposition. The focus is on armed conflict involving consciously conducted and planned political campaigns rather than spontaneous violence. (3.3) Dyad: A dyad consists of two conflicting primary parties. At least one of the primary parties must be the government of a state. In interstate conflicts, both primary parties 1For a more in-depth discussion on definitions, see http://www.pcr.uu.se/research/ucdp/definitions/. 2 Note that an incompatibility involving two opposition groups, each involved in clashes with the government resulting in 20 deaths, would not be recorded as a conflict (neither dyad reached the minimum casualty threshold), whereas an incompatibility involving a single opposition group that caused 25 battle-deaths would be included in the dataset. 1 are state governments.3 In intrastate and extrasystemic conflicts, the non-governmental primary party includes one or more opposition organization(s). A conflict can include more than one dyad. If e.g. a government is opposed by three rebel groups over the same incompatibility, the conflict is made up of three dyads. Note that secondary parties (i.e. intervening states supplying troops to one of the primary parties) do not lead to the formation of additional dyads. (4) State: A state is an internationally recognised sovereign government controlling a specific territory or an internationally unrecognised government controlling a specified territory whose sovereignty is not disputed by another internationally recognized sovereign government previously controlling the same territory. See Section 4.5 for details on the sample of countries covered by this definition. (5) Incompatibility concerning government or territory: The incompatibility, as stated by the parties, must concern government and/or territory. (5.1) Incompatibility: The stated general incompatible positions. (5.2) Incompatibility concerning government: Incompatibility concerning type of political system, the replacement of the central government, or the change of its composition. (5.3) Incompatibility concerning territory: Incompatibility concerning the status of a territory, e.g. the change of the state in control of a certain territory (interstate conflict), secession or autonomy (internal conflict). 3With three exceptions, the primary parties in interstate conflicts consist of only one actor on each side (and thus only constitute one dyad). See description of Location (Section 4.1) below for further information on these cases. 2 3 Variables in the Armed Conflict Dataset The observation (or unit) in the dataset is the conflict-year. Each conflict is listed in all years where fighting in one or more dyad(s) caused at least 25 battle-related deaths.4 The calendar year is the basic unit of every observation. Thus, if a conflict during the period June– September results in 30 casualties, that year will be recorded as a year of conflict. However, if the same number of casualties occurred in the period November–February and the conflict failed to reach the threshold of 25 battle-related deaths in either calendar year, neither year will be coded as in conflict. This has a number of consequences that will be discussed below. Start dates frequently refer to years prior to the first calendar year of a conflict, as the start of a conflict might be in a year with less than 25 fatalities. Small conflicts might not be included. Certain observations might be based on a single event, such as the Omagh bombing in Northern Ireland in 1998, which exceeded the minimum threshold for armed conflict. This is the country whose government or territory is disputed. For certain conflicts, such as Kurdistan, the disputed territory is divided between different countries. Following our definition, we have coded separate conflicts for each country.  For interstate conflict, all primary parties are listed in the Location field. Even if several governments are involved in the conflict, only countries that fulfil the inclusion criteria for primary actors are listed here. This normally means that two countries are listed, but there are four notable exceptions: In the Arab-Israeli war of 1948–49 as well as the Suez war of 7 1956, the war in Afghanistan in 2001 and the war in Iraq in 2003, there are more than two primary parties to the conflict.  For extrasystemic conflicts, Location is set to be the disputed area, not the government of the colonial power. Since the Location field in these conflicts by default does not indicate members of the international system, it constitutes an exception from the definition presented in Section 2. 4.2 Incompatibility As a country can experience several simultaneous conflicts, it is essential to differentiate between them. As described in Section 2.1, UCDP collects information on conflicts where the incompatibility, i.e. the general incompatible positions, concerns either government, territory or both. Early versions of the UCDP/PRIO dataset only contained two incompatibility categories, territory and government. Conflicts that concerned both territory and government were assigned to their primary incompatibility. From Version 4-2007, the incompatibility has been coded in three categories: 1. Territory 2. Government 3. Government AND Territory Note that the incompatibility expressed in terms of government or a specific territory is crude in the sense that possible underlying incompatibilities are not considered. In other words, the stated incompatibility is what the parties are (or claim to be) fighting over, but it says nothing about why the parties are fighting. While a state can only experience one intrastate conflict over government in a given year, that same state can simultaneously be a primary party to one or more interstate conflicts over government and/or territory. In the case of intrastate territorial conflicts, multiple conflicts can be recorded over different territories in a state in a given year. 4.3 Start dates temporal precision7 The Start date is coded as precisely as possible. For certain conflicts we can pinpoint the start of the armed conflict down to a single event, taking place on a specific day. For other conflicts, this is not possible, due to lack of precise information. The start precision is coded to highlight the level of certainty for the date set in the start_date variable. 1. Day, month and year are precisely coded; we have good information on the event. 2. Day is assigned; month and year are precisely coded. The assigned date can either be one of several events that can be classified as the first; it can be the last day in a period when 7 The format for coding start dates has been slightly changed in 2014, and then again in 2017, in an attempt to provide more detailed information. 8 several fatalities have been reported jointly or it can be an event that different sources claim occurred on different dates. 3. Day is unknown; month (or a period of 30 days, not necessarily a calendar month) and year are precisely coded. The day is known to be in a given month or 30 day-period, but we are missing information on an exact date. Day is then set to the last day of the period. 4. Month is assigned; year is coded precisely. 5. Day and month are unknown, year is coded precisely. Day and month are set as precisely as possible. For example, if an event is known to have taken place sometime between January and August, the date is coded as 31 August of the coded year, with a precision of 5. 6. Year is assigned. There is a wide disagreement between different sources, so that not even year can be coded precisely. The start year is assigned based on subjective judgment. Day and month are set as precisely as possible. For example, if an event is known to have taken place sometime between January and August in an assigned year, the date is coded as 31 August, with a precision of 6. 7. Year is missing. No reliable information on the start year is available. Day and month are set as precisely as possible for the first year of recorded activity. For example, if an event is known to have taken place sometime between January and August in an assigned year, the date is coded as 31 August, with a precision of 7. 4.4 Episode end dates temporal precision The end_date is coded as precisely as possible. For certain conflicts we can pinpoint the termination of the armed conflict down to a single event, taking place on a specific day.
